sentences.text:
This is the first bail application filed by the applicant under Section 483 of BNSS for grant of regular bail relating to Crime No.263/2020 registered at Police Station - Kolar Road, District Bhopal (M.P.)
for the offence punishable under Sections 420, 34 of the IPC.

entities.text: Police Station - Kolar Road, District Bhopal
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
Applicant is in detention since 28.01.2024.
2.

As per the prosecution story, the allegation against the applicant is that a written complaint was made by the complainant Ramlata Khandelwal with the allegation that in the year 2015,
complainant entered into a registered agreement with Krishna Builders for purchase of plot no.23 to 49 in Agrawal Phase-II. That prior to purchase information was published and in such unit namely Agrawal Phase-II, it is alleged that Jyoti Agrawal was a partner.
That the partner namely Sunil Agrawal requested that the validity of the registered agreement be extended for a period of one year.

That NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:1164 2 MCRC-39188-2024 subsequent to such sale by means of agreement to the complainant, another notice of information was published by the complainant in which the co- accused person submitted objection and thus, it is alleged that since Smt. Jyoti Agrawal is alleged to be a partner in Krishna Builders, the said objection was filed on behalf of her son and thus an offence under Section 420 of IPC has been alleged against the present applicant.
Therefore, the case was registered against the present applicant and other co-accused persons.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the case.
Applicant is in jail since 28.01.2024.
Co-accused Sunil Tibrewal has been enlarged on bail by the co- ordinate Bench of this Court in connection with Crime No.RC0082022A0004 vide order dated 07.11.2024 in MCRC No.39056 of 2024.

sentences.text: The trial of the case will take considerable time.
Therefore, it has been prayed that the applicant may be released on bail pending the trial.
4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the State has opposed the grant of bail to the applicant.
5. Having taken into consideration all the facts and circumstances of the case, but without commenting on merits of the case, I am inclined to release the applicant on bail.

Consequently, bail application under Section 483 of B.N.S.S./439 of Cr.P.C. for grant of bail filed on behalf of applicant,
stands allowed.

6. It is directed that the applicant shall be released on bail subject to NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:1164 3 MCRC-39188-2024 fulfilling the conditions mentioned in the agreement and on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.

He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 480(3) of B.N.S.S.
7.
This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case of bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
Certified copy as per rules.

(PRAMOD KUMAR AGRAWAL) JUDGE SSL Sunil Tibrewal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119347162/
